mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from deep contraction indicates a durable return of commuting and daytime population, which lifts retail-and-recreation footfall and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -39.1 to -14.0 and WORKPLACES rose from -37.3 to -29.0 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to rise or holding their gains.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT crossing above -15% signals that mobility restrictions have eased enough to restore discretionary trips; retail-and-recreation then follows transit upward over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: After TRANSIT rises above -15%, the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous above-baseline PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM activity shows households are combining outdoor leisure with errands, a behavioral bundle that spills into retail-and-recreation spending and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is +11.9% and GROCERY_PHARM is +6.9% at t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both remain above their pre-period baselines, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days fails to exceed its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an imminent easing of emergency restrictions, the still-positive RESIDENTIAL series will decline as people leave home more; this release of stay-at-home intensity drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from +3.3 to +2.6 while TRANSIT improved to -14.0
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below +2.5% and TRANSIT keeps rising, but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: High GROCERY_PHARM and above-baseline RESIDENTIAL indicate persistent home-centric routines; as these routines delay the return to discretionary shopping, RETAIL_REC declines over the next week relative to its recent level.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above +5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is +6.9% and RESIDENTIAL is +2.6% at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5% and RESIDENTIAL above +2%, but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than or equal to its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The decline in PARKS from its summer peak as autumn begins shifts leisure spending from outdoor parks to indoor retail-and-recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from +16.3 to +11.9 while RETAIL_REC held near -18
regime_hint: seasonal transition from summer to autumn
failure_condition: If PARKS falls below +12% but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of TRANSIT above -15% and GROCERY_PHARM above +5% confirms that both commuting and errand activity are recovering; this broad reopening bundle accelerates retail-and-recreation recovery over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -14.0 and GROCERY_PHARM is +6.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT is above -15% and GROCERY_PHARM is above +5%, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than or equal to its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A WORKPLACES crossing above -28% signals that office occupancy has turned the corner; the resulting weekday footfall lifts retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -37.3 to -29.0 and is near the -28% threshold
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises above -28% but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than its prior 14-day mean.
